body:
The humor comes from a recognizable human contradiction.

Warmth matters. The editorial checks screen for partisan attacks, cruelty, weak grammar and recycled punchlines.

title: A simple generation flow
steps: Enter a city, a state and a cartoon count. Generate saves the request before production starts.
Dated sources guide the subject. The writer and reviewer revise the caption and matching TV and menu ideas.
The RTX 4090 creates TV art. The compositor preserves the room and matching cast, then adds chalk and dialogue.
The bar follows real production stages. Finished images appear automatically with downloads and source records.

title: The system behind the screen
steps: GitHub holds the website code and selected art. Vercel serves the website and authenticated request endpoints.
The database retains the queue, job state and receipts. Private storage holds generated images and evidence.
A worker polls for due jobs and runs local models. Requests wait while the studio is offline. Completed steps have recovery checkpoints.
A dedicated always-on GPU machine can take over production. It will still need monitoring, storage and recovery testing.

title: Print size changes the detail
body:
The source is 1024 x 1536 pixels. Enlarging the picture does not create new detail.

The website exports exact-size PDFs on Letter or A4. Use Actual size in the print dialog and confirm the publication’s requirements.

title: An editor’s view
subtitle: Cartoons, slides and newspaper layouts
body:
The Presentation tab browses all 40 cartoons in full-screen slides.

Choose up to 12 cartoons for a print packet. Compare four artwork sizes or switch on the 11 x 17 inch newspaper layout study.

Every generated edition still needs editorial review before publication.
